APPLY [AAAA] EDS | | BRAIN Tableau AD Login Failed on events which are detected by the LOCAL system
AND when the event(s) were detected by one or more of Business Research Analytics Insights Network modules
AND when BB:BRAIN Tableau AD Logon attempt match at least 1 times with the same Obfuscated String (custom) in 1 minutes after BB:BRAIN Tableau Multiple failed match with the same Obfuscated String (custom)
final_rule:
rule brain_tableau_rapid_login_failures {
  meta:
    author = "Your Name"
    description = "Detect rapid logon attempts following multiple failed logins in the BRAIN Tableau system indicating a potential security threat."
    severity = "High"
    created = "2023-10-23"

  events:
    any (
      $failed_logon_attempts.event_type = "failed_logon_attempt" and
      $failed_logon_attempts.detection_source in ["LOCAL system", "Business Research Analytics Insights Network modules"] and
      $failed_logon_attempts.logon_type = "BB:BRAIN Tableau Multiple failed"
    )

  match:
    when $failed_logon_attempts over 1m {
      $grouped_attempts = group_by($failed_logon_attempts, "Obfuscated String (custom)")
      aggregate($grouped_attempts, count(*) >= 1)
    }
}

suppression_window
The suppression_window option lets you control how often a rule triggers a detection. It
prevents the same rule from generating multiple detections within a specified time window,
even if the rule's conditions are met multiple times. Suppression windowing uses a
tumbling window approach, which suppresses duplicates over a fixed-size, non-overlapping
window.
You can optionally provide a suppression_key to further refine which instances of the rule
are suppressed within the suppression window. If not specified, all instances of the rule are
suppressed. This key is defined as an outcome variable.
In the following example, suppression_window is set to 5m and suppression_key is set to
the $hostname variable. After the rule triggers a detection for $hostname, any further
detections for $hostname are suppressed for the next five minutes. However, if the rule
triggers on an event with a different hostname, a detection is created.
The default value of suppression_window is 0; that is, the suppression window is disabled
by default. This option only works for single event rules
(/chronicle/docs/detection/yara-l-2-0-overview#single-event-rule) that don't have a match section.
Example:
Composite detection rules
rule SuppressionWindowExample {
  // Other rule sections
  outcome:
    $suppression_key = $hostname
  options:
    suppression_window = 5m
}
